name: KRAFTON Raon-1 nano
context_scaling: Native 262,144 tokens. config.json sets mla_use_nope: true and rope_parameters: null, so the 6 gated-MLA layers carry no positional encoding at all - there is no rope_scaling block because there is no rope. The 18 Raon Delta Attention layers are recurrent with a fixed-size state, which is where length behaviour comes from instead. Card states 'Position Encoding: NoPE' and 262,144 native; no window beyond that is claimed.
attention_variant: Hybrid RDA 3:1 with gated MLA, from config.json: mla_layers [4,8,12,16,20,24] (1-indexed on the card, so 0-indexed 3,7,11,15,19,23) are the only 6 layers that hold a per-token KV cache, and rda_layers covers the other 18 with Raon Delta Attention (gated delta-rule linear attention, separate erase and write gates, fixed-size recurrent state). The MLA cache is latent, not per-head: kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64 = 576 floats/token/layer, so num_kv_heads is recorded as 1 and head_dim as 576 to express that latent rather than a per-head geometry. Raon-mHC residual with 4 streams (raon_mhc_streams 4). Card: '16 attention heads for RDA; 32 for Gated MLA', 'Attention Head Dimension 128 for RDA; 192 QK / 128 V for Gated MLA'.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-12 from the HF trending feed (rank ~24, 58 downloads, 62 likes at crawl). A trained-from-scratch Korean/English model by KRAFTON AI, NOT a derivative: the mHC/RDA stack is its own. It IS derived by MoE-to-Dense pruning from the catalog's raon-1-mini-preview (30B-A4B) per the card's Training section (arXiv 2605.28207), then continued pre-training on 3T tokens - so it is a distinct record, not a fine-tune, and base_model is deliberately left unset because it is a new architecture, not a post-train of that checkpoint. PARAMS: HF safetensors total 3,529,911,376 (BF16 3,529,874,224 + F32 37,152) = 3.53B, which includes the 55M MTP module. The card's own figures are '3.1B main model + 55M MTP = 3.2B checkpoint' and '1.5B effective parameters (3.1B total, including a 1.5B per-layer embedding table)'. active_params_b is recorded as 1.5 because the per-layer embedding table is a lookup, not matmul, so generation compute tracks the 1.5B slice: flops_per_token_active = 2 x 1.5e9 = 3.0e9. Memory footprint is the full 3.53B. KV: the card claims 'about 7 KiB per token in BF16' and the arithmetic agrees - 6 cache-holding layers x (512 + 64) x 2 bytes = 6,912 B/token, and the other 18 layers are constant-state. That is the reason this record matters for a low-VRAM box: 262,144 tokens costs ~1.8 GiB of cache rather than the ~26 GiB a 24-layer GQA(16/4, head_dim 128) dense stack would need. EVIDENCE: the card's benchmark HTML table compares against Qwen3.5-2B, Gemma 4 E2B (5.1B total / E2.3B), MiniCPM5-2B and LFM3-1.7B. It wins IFBench 75.9 vs 73.7 (LFM3) and 63.8 (MiniCPM5), FACTS Grounding 44.4 vs 13.8 (Qwen3.5-2B), PersonaMem v2 38.8 vs 29.2, PrefEval 44.0 vs 26.1, and the Korean rows by wide margins (Chatbot Korean 91.0 vs 42.2). It LOSES MMLU-Redux to MiniCPM5-2B 84.0 (81.1 for nano), BFCL v4 to LFM3 67.2 (56.3), NL2SH to Gemma 4 E2B 62.6 (58.0) and BrowseComp Plus to MiniCPM5 37.2 (34.5). CAVEATS: every number is vendor-run. The card names per-benchmark sampling settings (temp 0.7 knowledge, 1.0 tool use, 0.1 + presence 1.5 elsewhere) but prints no harness build and no compile (SGLang/vLLM/llama.cpp) for the table; three benchmarks are internal (Office Work Bench, Chatbot Korean) and one is a 32k-context setting (PersonaMem v2), so cross-card comparison is indicative only. Rows are recorded only where a peer column exists in the same table.
